findings.title: Place the available Charismatic recruit before Turmoil

summary_evidence.exact: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

**Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** Each card requires:
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

findings.explanation: The official full FAQ explicitly requires placing the one available warrior before Turmoil. The summary repeats unconditional immediate Turmoil whenever full completion is impossible, specifically including warrior supply. The general maximum-placement statement does not clearly resolve this order. This can leave a required warrior incorrectly in supply. This is operational ambiguity/omission rather than an explicit sentence saying place zero.
findings.correct_result: With Charismatic, one warrior available and a legal matching roost: place that warrior, then Turmoil because recruitment was not fully completed; do not continue Decree.

findings.title: Allied Woodland Alliance warriors do not cause Outrage when forced into sympathy

summary_evidence.exact: - **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.

source_refs: p16 TXT 490–492 and 609–611 (Allied Alliance Outrage FAQ)
p16 TXT 39–41 (Use of Force), 472 (Outrage), 618 (Moving with Ally)
findings.explanation: The summary unconditionally says moving Allied warriors into sympathy triggers Outrage. The FAQ explicitly says this is false when those warriors belong to the Woodland Alliance: Allied movement forces the faction to move its warriors, so it is not another player moving into its own sympathetic clearing. The mistaken statement creates an unwarranted card payment/draw.
findings.correct_result: Force Allied Alliance warriors into sympathy without Outrage. The general Outrage rule still applies for other Allied factions moved into sympathy.

findings.title: An already-dominant player cannot be chosen as a coalition partner

summary_evidence.exact: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

findings.explanation: The summary lists coalition partner eligibility but does not exclude a player who already activated dominance. The FAQ explicitly excludes that player because they have no score marker on the track. Without the exclusion, a player may use their former numerical VP to select an illegal partner. The summary correctly allows a legal existing partner to activate dominance later and win that way; that is a separate sequence.
findings.correct_result: Choose the eligible lowest-scoring noncoalition player still on the VP track; do not form a new coalition with an already-dominant player. A coalition partner can activate dominance afterward.
